subject: Tenant control requirements — discovery summary & engineering asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@acme.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant control requirements — discovery summary & engineering asks

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. I promised to capture a short, actionable recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps for the technical deep-dive we discussed. Below is what I heard from the group and a few clarifying questions.

1) Pain points (what you shared)
- No per-customer throughput guarantees today — the biggest issue is unpredictable noisy neighbors during marketing spikes.
- Lack of tenant-tiering controls: we can’t reliably restrict feature/throughput levels per customer.
- Auditability and billing fidelity: need per-org metrics (tokens, requests, KV cache hits) for invoicing and SRE investigations.
- Data residency / EU pinning — certain enterprise accounts require EU-only processing.

2) Current stack (as described)
- Fronting APIs in GKE + internal API gateway; model endpoints are self-hosted on a mix of AWS EC2 instances with autoscaling groups.
- Redis used for short-term cache; long-term telemetry pushed to internal Prometheus + ClickHouse.
- Customers identified by X-Org-ID header.

3) Success criteria (what would make this successful for Acme)
- Tier1 customers: p95 generation latency < 150ms for common prompts and guaranteed baseline throughput during spikes.
- Ability to apply per-tenant rate limits and quota buckets (monthly and burst credits).
- Region pinning (EU) for selected org_ids and proof of residency for audit.
- Centralized audit logs showing per-org token counts and cache hit rates for billing and compliance.

4) Proposed Redwood capabilities relevant to these needs (high level)
- Per-tenant rate limiting & quota profiles with tiered defaults + transient burst credits.
- Request routing policies to pin traffic to region-specific clusters (EU pinning) and fallback policies for availability.
- Token-level telemetry and cost attribution exported to your billing pipeline (we can map by X-Org-ID).
- Admin controls for creating/adjusting tier assignments and emergency overrides.

5) Clarifying/questions
- For EU pinning: are there specific accounts with contractual language requiring in-region processing, or is this a general preference?
- For billing: do you prefer CSV exports to your S3 bucket or a push to your billing API?
- Can you share a short sample of X-Org-ID values (sanitized) so we can validate attribute mapping in the deep-dive?

6) Next steps / owner assignments
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (60–75m) with Dev (solutions engineer) and our infra lead. Proposed slots: Thu 2/19 10:00–11:15 PT or Fri 2/20 08:00–09:15 PT. (Action: Emma/Tom to confirm)
- I’ll send a short one-pager outlining the tenant controls pattern and a checklist of artifacts we’ll ask for ahead of the deep-dive (auth header examples, sample telemetry, and a small test payload). (Owner: Aditya)
- If procurement needs SOC2 evidence ahead of the deep-dive, flag below and I’ll route to our security team.

Attachment: redwood-tenant-controls-one-pager.pdf (one-page summary + architecture diagram)

Thanks — appreciate the time today. I’ll update the HubSpot deal and push the one-pager to the shared drive.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Call notes excerpt:
On the call: Emma Rogers (Acme), Tom Greene (Acme infra), Marissa Cole (Redwood AE), Aditya Rao (Redwood SE).
Key quote: "We need something that guarantees performance for our highest-value customers during campaign bursts — we can’t afford noisy neighbor regressions."
From: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@acme.co>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme.co>, procurement <procure@acme.co>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant control requirements — discovery summary & engineering asks

Aditya —

Thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A couple of updates and one ask:

- Burst credits: we do need a mechanism to allocate limited burst capacity for marketing campaigns that only certain org_ids can consume. Ideally those are consumed first-in, first-out and have simple admin controls so our CS team can grant/revoke quickly.
- Data residency: several of our enterprise customers are EU-only. That is contractual for two accounts (org_83 and org_99) — we will need contractual language as part of the procurement flow.
- Billing exports: CSV to an S3 bucket is preferred.

One ask: can you share your SOC 2 Type II report or an equivalent security posture doc for procurement? I’ve attached a short procurement checklist.

Thanks — I’ll confirm availability for the deep-dive (I prefer Thu 2/19 10:00 PT).

Best,
Emma Rogers
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
emma.rogers@acme.co

Attachment: acme-procurement-checklist.xlsx

Emma / Tom —

Appreciate the quick confirmation and the procurement checklist. Quick responses inline + next steps: 

- Burst credits: Yes — Redwood supports burst-credit pools that can be assigned to specific org_ids. They are tokenized and consumed against a tenant bucket; CS/admins can grant/revoke via the Console and we expose an API for programmatic control. We’ll show the admin flow in the deep-dive and can demo a campaign allocation as a quick proof.

- EU pinning / contractual language: We can support EU-only processing and provide a SOC2 Type II attestation and the standard EU data residency addendum for your contracts. I’ll copy our security liaison if procurement needs a direct email.

- Billing exports: CSV to S3 is straightforward — we can include per-org token counts, request counts, and a cache-hit column. We’ll map X-Org-ID to the org label you provide.

Technical prep for the deep-dive (items we’d like ahead of the meeting to speed things up):
- A sanitized sample of X-Org-ID values (3–5 examples).
- A short example of a typical request payload (headers + body) and the approximate size distribution (short vs long prompts).
- Any SLOs you currently track for inference (p50/p95/p99) and typical traffic patterns during a marketing spike.

Proposed meeting: Thu 2/19 10:00–11:15 PT (Dev and infra lead on our side will join). Please confirm and I’ll send the calendar invite.

I’ve uploaded the one-pager and a short tenant-controls checklist to the shared drive (link below) and updated the HubSpot deal. If procurement needs the SOC2 file before the meeting, say the word and I’ll get it routed.

Links:
